subject: Insurance
title: Why American Healthcare Is So Expensive
description: A short lesson to help you apply Why American Healthcare Is So Expensive.

hook.text: The US spends $4.5 trillion on healthcare annually—$13,000 per person. No other country comes close.

buildup.text: Drug prices, administrative costs, and high provider salaries drive spending.

discovery.text: Administrative costs alone consume 30% of US spending. Insurance paperwork, billing, and coding eat $1 trillion a year.

twist.text: Despite spending the most, the US ranks last among wealthy nations in health outcomes.

climax.text: America's cost crisis isn't about too much care.

punchline.text: $4.5 trillion a year, worst outcomes. America pays the most and gets the least.

quiz.question: What is the largest driver of US healthcare administrative costs?
